---
title: "Screening in a state's counties, with rurality"
---

This is the same measure/release query the [Home](/index.qmd) map's data
was built from, scoped to one state: Colorado. Press **Run** and it executes
in your browser with DuckDB-Wasm against the latest release. Nothing runs until
you do.

Two things keep the read to a few megabytes of `measure.observation`, which is
one very large Parquet file. It is laid out by state first, so a
`geo_id LIKE 'county:08%'` filter (`08` is Colorado's FIPS code) lets DuckDB skip
every other state's row groups. And the filters on `source`, `source_release`
and `measure_id` narrow the rest. To look at another state, change `08` in
both places it appears.

Colorectal cancer screening in Colorado's counties, lowest first, with the
interval, its status and the county's rurality code (RUCC, 1 is most
metropolitan):

```{.sql .runnable}
SELECT u.name, o.value AS pct, o.lower, o.upper, o.value_status,
       r.value AS rucc_code
FROM measure.observation o
JOIN geography.unit u
  ON u.geo_id = o.geo_id AND u.vintage = 2026
LEFT JOIN measure.observation r
  ON r.geo_id = o.geo_id AND r.source = 'RUCC' AND r.geo_id LIKE 'county:08%'
WHERE o.source = 'PLACES' AND o.source_release = '2025'
  AND o.measure_id = 'PLACES:COLON_SCREEN:age_adjusted'
  AND o.geo_id LIKE 'county:08%' AND u.parent_geo_id = 'state:08'
ORDER BY pct
LIMIT 20
```

The same join, summarised by rurality code: how many counties sit at each
RUCC level, and their mean screening rate. (A chart would show the gradient
better; a table is what the page has for now.)

```{.sql .runnable}
SELECT r.value AS rucc_code, count(*) AS counties, round(avg(o.value), 1) AS mean_pct
FROM measure.observation o
JOIN measure.observation r
  ON r.geo_id = o.geo_id AND r.source = 'RUCC' AND r.geo_id LIKE 'county:08%'
WHERE o.source = 'PLACES' AND o.source_release = '2025'
  AND o.measure_id = 'PLACES:COLON_SCREEN:age_adjusted'
  AND o.geo_id LIKE 'county:08%'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
```

Other measures to swap in for `measure_id`: `PLACES:MAMMOUSE:age_adjusted`
(mammography use), `PLACES:CSMOKING:age_adjusted` (current smoking),
`PLACES:CHECKUP:age_adjusted` (annual checkup), `PLACES:CANCER:age_adjusted`
(cancer, non-skin, or melanoma). Use **Open in DuckDB Shell** to edit and run
a block yourself, or the [SQL playground](/playground.qmd).
